title: RunnerDispatchRequest
description:
The `agent-runner` `POST /dispatch` request body (agent-runner's own `DispatchInput`, `src/domain/run.ts`). Published so a caller in another language (Factory, Python) can validate against the exact proven wire shape instead of an opaque hand-rolled dict. Fulfils demand `factory-20260911-interface-extraction` criterion 2, and (for `dispatchKey`) demand `agent-runner-20260927-contracts-runner-keyed-dispatch` — additive only, no field here is new, every one is copied from the real, shipped TypeScript type.

**Two ways to correlate a dispatch, and they are not alternatives you may mix.**

1. **Keyed (`dispatchKey` present) — preferred.** The caller mints a `dispatchKey` and sends it with the request. The runner durably reserves it, bound to a `requestHash` and the minted run id, **before** spawning anything; a repeat of the same key with the same `requestHash` replays the existing run instead of starting a second one, and the same key with a *different* `requestHash` is refused with HTTP 409. Recovery after a lost response is then a single `GET /dispatches/{dispatchKey}` — see `runner.dispatch-reservation.json`, which also fixes the exact canonicalization `requestHash` is computed over. A keyed request is otherwise unchanged: an unkeyed request stays valid exactly as it was.

2. **Unkeyed (no `dispatchKey`) — today's behaviour, unchanged, weaker.** There is no idempotency contract at all in this case (spec-factory.md open question 2: 'agent-runner has no idempotency-key contract'). The proven, real convention a caller uses instead — see `factory.service.dispatch` — is to mint its own operation token (`<caller>-operation:<uuid>`) and embed it as the literal first line of `prompt`. See `runner.run-record.json` for how that token is later matched against a `RunnerRunRecord` to resolve what actually happened, without ever blindly resending. That match is a text scan over prompts and is strictly weaker than a keyed lookup: it is the fallback for callers that cannot mint a key, not a substitute for one.

repo.description: Functional name (D002) of the allow-listed repo to dispatch a session into. Non-allow-listed repos are rejected before any run starts.

prompt.description: The full dispatch prompt. See this schema's top-level description for the unkeyed operation-correlation convention (an operation token as the prompt's own first line) — agent-runner treats this as opaque text, so the convention is producer/consumer discipline, not schema-enforced structure. A keyed request does not need the token, and `prompt` remains required either way.

dispatchKey.description: OPTIONAL caller-minted idempotency key for this intended execution, 8–200 characters. Mint it once per intended execution and reuse the *same* key for every retry of that execution; mint a new key for a genuinely new execution. It is opaque to the runner (never parsed, never used as a run id) and is the caller's durable handle on the run: `GET /dispatches/{dispatchKey}` resolves a lost `POST /dispatch` response. The pattern admits the `<caller>-operation:<uuid>` token Factory already mints (e.g. `factory-operation:9f0e2b1a-1111-2222-3333-444455556666`), so a caller can use one token for both mechanisms. Omitting the field means the unkeyed behaviour above, unchanged.

demandId.description: The demand this session was dispatched to fulfill, when there is one (same shape as `demand.json`'s `id`). Recorded on the run and echoed into the `agent.run` state-event, but does not itself resolve a prompt in this chunk — `prompt` is still required.

model.description: Per-dispatch `--model` override. Omitted (not present at all) falls back to the runner's configured default; an explicit empty string means 'no `--model` argument', not 'use the default' — the two are different requests.

effort.description: Per-dispatch `--effort` override, same omitted-vs-explicit-value semantics as `model`.

runtime.description: Which configured inference backend/runtime profile to dispatch on. Omitted resolves from `model` if a profile claims it, else the configured default. An unrecognized name is rejected before any run starts, never silently defaulted.

workspace.description: OPTIONAL task workspace (demand `factory-20261018-contracts-runner-workspace`; agent-runner demand `factory-20261017-agent-runner-task-workspaces`). Asks the runner to run this dispatch in a temporary git worktree on its own task branch instead of the repository's main checkout, so two tasks of one app can run at once. Only an app repository (one whose `app.yaml` says it is an app) accepts it; a hexagon or platform repository is refused and keeps the single-session rule. ABSENT means a plain run, exactly as before: every existing request stays valid, and an absent `workspace` is left out of the `requestHash` field list (see `runner.dispatch-reservation.json`). The task is named by exactly one of `taskId` or `key` (the runner treats both as the same thing).

kind.description: The only workspace kind that exists: a git worktree for one task.

taskId.description: The task's id, for example `PLA-73`. Exactly one of `taskId` / `key`.

key.description: The task's key, for example `PLA-73`. Exactly one of `taskId` / `key`.

branch.description: The task branch, `feature/<KEY>-<slug>`: one `feature/` segment, then a conservative ref-safe tail. The runner additionally refuses `..`, a trailing `.`, `.lock` or `/`, and `//`.

base.description: What the branch is cut from: an integration branch name (for example `dev`) or a full 40-hex lowercase commit SHA (which this pattern also admits). Runner-side the same ref-safety refusals as `branch` apply.

reuse.description: `true`: reuse this task's existing worktree (a resume). `false`: refuse if one already exists.
